mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal records office of the director's country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory KYC/CDD per AMLA Art. 3-4 and FINMA Circular 2023/3: at least (a) identification of founders and any principal UBO; (b) screening against the SECO consolidated sanctions list (Swiss law), the UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC/SDN where the transaction involves US-dollar settlement rails or US correspondent banks, and EU restrictive measures; (c) PEP screening under Art. 2a AMLA and FATF R.12, with enhanced due diligence for PEP and PEP-family UBOs; (d) negative news and adverse-reputation screening via OECD and proprietary databases; (e) retention of CDD records for 10 years after termination of the business relationship (Art. 7 AMLA).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Business Name Index of the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office (SOGC/BJ, zefix.ch); filing is initiated through a Swiss notary using the eGRIS/iHandelsregister registration portal or the web-based Zefix name-check module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to Art. 950 CO and Art. 12-14 of the Commercial Register Ordinance (HRA, SR 221.411), the firm name must be expressed in one of the Swiss national languages (German, French, Italian, Romansh), with allowances for certain internationally recognizable Latin-script words; a Latin-script transliteration is obligatory for names originating in a non-Latin script (e.g., Chinese, Russian, Arabic); the name must correspond to the actual IVD manufacturing purpose, must not mislead as to scope or scale, and may contain descriptors such as 'Diagnostics', 'Point of Care', or 'Immunoassay' where the intended Swiss commercial purpose so reflects
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss / Suisse / Switzerland / Confederation / Helvetia (requires license from the Federal Institute of Intellectual Property)
International / Global / World (without registered genuine cross-border substance)
Fund / Fondation / SPV (misleading financial structure), and any token implying a state guarantee
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Swiss law provides no statutory name reservation window; once the notary files the name within the incorporation file, the official Commercial Register Office conducts compliance and distinctiveness checks. If the name is rejected, the notary receives a grounded written notice. Counsel may request reconsideration within 10 days and thereafter invoke the administrative instruction procedure before the cantonal Commercial Register supervisory authority (Art. 970a CO) within 30 days. Further appeal lies to the cantonal administrative court and finally to the Federal Supreme Court (Art. 82-89 BGG). Filing an appeal does not suspend adoption of an alternate name; a compliant alternate name may be registered in parallel, and the entire challenge procedure is practicably resolved within 45-75 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual-only offices (PO box or pure domiciliation without local material activity) are not permissible for a manufacturing AG that must hold a physical seat in a Swiss municipality (Art. 51-56 CO) and operate as the genuine point-of-care IVD production entity. A properly staffed commercial service-office arrangement (physical registered address, accessible place of administration, authorized mailbox, and unlimited power of attorney for service) is tolerated during pre-incorporation and early set-up, but Swiss federal practice requires actual management substance at the registered seat (payroll, bookkeeping, management or a qualified local agent) to avoid tax treaty-override, de facto liquidation, and Swissmedic licensing risks.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 30% probability of an unannounced commercial/tax/social security inspection during the first 24 months at the registered office; the likelihood rises to 55-70% once a Swissmedic Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) license for IVD equipment is triggered, which entails mandatory premises inspections and customs post-clearance checks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO) arts. 626–643 (incorporation of the Aktiengesellschaft), arts. 716a–716b (non-transferable board duties), art. 629 (share subscription and payment), art. 642 (minimum capital and paid-up amount), and art. 643 (registered office).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce), acting under the Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV) of the Swiss Federal Department of Justice and Police.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Entry in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister / Requête d'inscription au registre du commerce).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Aktiengesellschaft requires minimum share capital of CHF 100,000, fully subscribed and issued; at least CHF 50,000 (i.e., 20% of the total capital, but not less than this floor) must be cash-paid up before registration, evidenced by a blocking certificate (Sperrbescheinigung) issued by a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank or securities dealer; the remaining must be fully paid within three years.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Company is incorporated as an Aktiengesellschaft under Swiss law with share capital and Articles of Association as approved by the shareholders. RESOLVED that all subscribed shares are hereby taken up and that the statutory minimum paid-up capital has been deposited to the Company's escrow account, as evidenced by the blocking certificate. RESOLVED that the registered office is established at the address recorded in the Commercial Register filing. RESOLVED that the following officers are elected: Chairman of the Board, Secretary, and Managing Officers. RESOLVED that the Chairman is authorized to execute and submit the incorporation application to the competent Commercial Register Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Apostilled Director Identity Documents and Notarized Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Cantonal Notary Public (Amtsnotariat / Office du notaire)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare notarial deed of the Articles of Association (Statuten) and the shareholders' subscription. Deliver original passport/CV for each founder and proposed board member; the notary authenticates the founding resolutions and certifies legal capacity.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each founder and board member
Articles of Association certified in accordance with art. 629 OR
Declaration of acceptance by each board member
Power of attorney if representation is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the articles, amend the document to correct deficiencies and re-execute before the same notary; no additional corporate action required unless substantive shareholder rights change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Escrow Account and Deposit Minimum Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss Bank or Securities Firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocking account (Sperrkonto) in the Company's name, transfer the cash capital, and obtain the bank's blocking certificate confirming the deposit is irrevocably reserved for the Company.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association
Provisional Commercial Register extract or confirmation of name reservation
Beneficial owner declaration (company and tax forms)
Identification of all signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires further compliance, provide refreshed corporate documents or an external legal opinion on the company legal structure; escalate to the bank's onboarding committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the official application form (Anmeldung) and compile all statutory exhibits, including the blocking certificate, notarized articles, board declaration, and specimen signatures. Execute the application with notarized signatures of authorised board members.
required_dossiers: Completed Anmeldung form
Notarized Articles of Association
Bank blocking certificate (Sperrbescheinigung)
List of directors and authorized signatories with specimen signatures
Declaration of compliance with capital requirements per art. 642 OR
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register issues a rectification request, cure the defect within 10 days by submitting corrected forms or supplementary declarations; appeal to the cantonal supervisory authority if the register refuses entry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Application for Entry in the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the full application electronically or in person, pay the cantonal court fee and registration fee, and verify that all signatures are notarized. The Register reviews the legal validity and compliance with minimum capital before issuing the Certificate of Commercial Register Entry.
required_dossiers: Complete application dossier (Step 3)
Proof of payment of registration fees
Any required expert report or audit confirmation if statutory capital contributions in kind are used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Register imposes conditions or suspends entry, submit a memorandum of law demonstrating compliance; use the formal appeal process (Beschwerde) before the cantonal civil court within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) and Cantonal Tax Administration; AHV/SUVA and Cantonal Compensation Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the company is entered, obtain the enterprise identification number (UID), register for VAT (MWST/TVA) with ESTV if annual worldwide turnover exceeds CHF 100,000, register with the cantonal tax office for corporate income tax and capital tax, and register employees with the AHV compensation office (AXA/Asga etc.) for social security.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register entry certificate
UID confirmation letter
VAT registration form (Formulaire MWST) if applicable
Employee registration form AHV
Board and shareholder resident identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registrations are delayed or rejected, request a retroactive effective date in the registration form, or file a formal application for late registration exemption with the competent tax office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products (Swissmedic), Bundesinstitut für Arzneimittel und Medizinprodukte; for devices, also the Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH/BAG) in the framework of the Therapeutic Products Act (TPA/HMG).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Establishment Authorization for the Manufacture of In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices (Herstellungsbewilligung für In-vitro-Diagnostika / Autorisation de fabrication de dispositifs médicaux de diagnostic in vitro) under art. 14 of the Swiss Therapeutic Products Act (HMG/TPA).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) in cooperation with the Cantonal Environmental Protection Department (Kantonales Amt für Umwelt)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Screening and classification under the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV/OEIE); typical production facilities with certain chemical storage or wastewater thresholds fall under Annex II category, requiring a simplified environmental impact report (Bericht/ Rapport EIE), otherwise registration and exemption from a full EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet the limits of the Swiss Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV) and the Wastewater Ordinance (VwV/ODa), including pH 6.5–9.5, BOD5 ≤ 20 mg/l, and prohibition of priority hazardous substances; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions must comply with the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV/OACI) total VOC concentration limits (mass flow-dependent), and hazardous waste handling must follow the Technical Ordinance on Waste (TVA/OTD) and the Guideline on Biological and Chemical Waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory fire safety certification from the cantonal fire prevention authority (Kantonaler Feuerpolizei/VKF) based on building load-bearing and escape route inspection; occupational clearance from the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) and SUVA for workplace safety, sanitation, and infection-control measures, including a hazard analysis and protective measures for handling biological or chemical reagents under the Swiss Labour Law (ArG).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung – ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions – AFC), Main Division Value Added Tax; official electronic portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; UID register: https://www.uid.ch
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. The Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) is the central business tax identification number. A Swiss AG obtains the UID automatically upon registration in the Commercial Register (Handelsregister). 2. A foreign entity without a Swiss branch must apply for a UID through the UID Register (www.uid.ch) by filing the 'Request for issue of UID for foreign entities' with the Swiss Federal Statistical Office, attaching certified evidence of foreign corporate registration, articles of association, proof of Swiss VAT-relevant activity, and a power of attorney appointing a Swiss fiscal representative. 3. Concurrently, the foreign entity must submit the VAT registration form to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (SFTA/ESTV), indicating audited turnover expectations in Switzerland and appointing a Swiss fiscal representative with Swiss domicile. 4. The SFTA issues the VAT identification number in the format CHE-123.456.789 MWST, which is used for invoicing, VAT returns, and export zero-rating claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Swiss federal law; an AG is always taxed as a separate legal entity at federal, cantonal, and communal levels. Available statutory elections include the VAT group election (Organschaft under Art. 22 VAT Act), cantonal tax status elections such as holding company and mixed/domicile company regimes (subject to phase-out restrictions effective 2020), and the election to apply the notional interest deduction on equity. For hybrid mismatch arrangements, Swiss tax classification is based on statutory legal form; a foreign-law check-the-box designation has no Swiss domestic tax effect, and Swiss anti-hybrid measures follow OECD/BEPS alignment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Federal Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 250,000 of annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies (Art. 10 para. 2 lit. a Swiss VAT Act); for foreign suppliers without Swiss domicile, the threshold is measured on Swiss turnover and a Swiss fiscal representative is mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control (CTC). Electronic invoices are legally recognised provided they guarantee authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility under Art. 26a VAT Act. The QR-bill payment slip standard is mandatory for payment slips on open invoices; electronic invoices in the Swiss eBill/XML format are customary. No digital stamping or pre-clearance approval is required; however, exporters must maintain a Swiss SAF-T (Audit File) compatible accounting archive for audit readiness.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated treatment for Swiss VAT applies to the export of goods when the goods are physically transported or dispatched to a foreign country and the recipient is abroad, as proven by a customs export declaration. Services performed directly on, or in connection with, exported goods, and certain services supplied to recipients with place of supply outside Switzerland, are also zero-rated. The supplier must hold verifiable documentary evidence showing that the goods left the Swiss customs territory or that the service is attributable to an external place of supply; otherwise the standard 8.1% rate must be charged.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Swiss customs export declaration via Passar/ETariff, including the export notification)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of the foreign currency consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration may reassess zero-rated exports within a 5-year limitation period, extended to 10 years in cases of confirmed tax evasion or serious documentary deficiency (Art. 72 VAT Act). If the export evidence or payment documentation is found deficient, the 0% rate is retrospectively reversed and the outstanding VAT of 8.1% is collected with default interest. For intentional underpayment of VAT, a penalty of up to three times the evaded tax may be imposed under Art. 100 VAT Act; for negligent conduct, penalties of up to one time the evaded tax apply. The Swiss customs authorities may also impose separate customs sanctions for false declarations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB); the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) for banking and AML/CFT supervision; the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) for trade policy and export controls; and the Anti-Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland (MROS) for suspicious transaction reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full capital and current account convertibility under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. There are no exchange controls, no central bank authorisation requirements for foreign currency transactions, and no restrictions on profit remittance, dividend repatriation, or capital withdrawal. CHF, EUR, USD and all major trade currencies are freely convertible in both directions without licence. The only regulatory frictions are (i) the 35% Swiss anticipatory withholding tax on Swiss-source dividends, which is refundable or reducible under an applicable double taxation treaty; (ii) SNB direct reporting obligations for balance-of-payments statistics whenever external assets or liabilities exceed CHF 2 million or annual external payments exceed CHF 1 million; and (iii) the statutory duty of Swiss banks to verify the economic background of every transaction under Article 7 of the Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG/AMLA), including documentary proof of the underlying commercial purpose of treasury flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None exist under Swiss law. There is no mandatory surrender rule, no statutory conversion timeline, and no forced repatriation quota for export receipts. A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft may retain export proceeds in any fully convertible currency in domestic or foreign bank accounts. The only binding obligations are commercial bookkeeping and account documentation under Articles 957 et seq. of the Swiss Code of Obligations (CO), plus the SNB direct-reporting thresholds to the Swiss National Bank for external assets, external liabilities, and annual foreign payment flows. No conversion ratio or liquidation of foreign currency balances is ever mandated.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto / compte de consignation) for the issuance of the Gründungsbestätigung under CO Art. 634; Operational multi-currency Current Account in CHF, EUR and USD
Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) for verification of paid-in share capital; Operational Current Account with SIC, SEPA and SWIFT rails in CHF, EUR and USD
Capital Escrow Account (compte de consignation) and Corporate Operating Account with full trade finance, documentary collections, and commercial letters of credit services
Commercial Current Account with foreign currency sub-accounts; Capital Escrow Account available for SME-oriented structures

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for the required CHF treasury, escrow, and LC-clearing functions. Non-Swiss offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not supervised by FINMA, cannot access the Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) system as direct participants, and cannot issue genuine CH IBANs for payroll, tax, or utility payments routed through SIC. A Swiss FinTech licence under Article 1b of the Swiss Banking Act allows only limited public deposit-taking and does not authorise credit granting, commercial letters of credit, or trade finance. Licensed Swiss digital banks may be used only as ancillary payroll and petty-cash accounts; the principal escrow, operational, and cross-border settlement relationship must reside with a full commercial bank under Swiss banking supervision.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in substance, with limited remote exceptions. FINMA Circular 2020/1 and the FINMA AML Ordinance require the bank to identify the contracting party, the beneficial owner, and the economic background. For a newly incorporated AG with non-resident shareholders, Swiss systemically relevant banks will require the Swiss-resident director (or, failing that, each ultimate beneficial owner) to appear physically at onboarding. Certified video-identification is accepted for individual authorised signatories only where the bank has already performed a face-to-face corporate visit, and some banks refuse remote opening entirely for mid-risk IVD manufacturers. The capital-release instruction and the verification of the founder’s declaration (Gründungsbestätigung) must be executed in an authenticated session, and the bank will require original or apostilled corporate documents for any foreign shareholder before the account is activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) chain opacity caused by layered foreign holding vehicles or nominee shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss Commercial Register excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug); articles of association with share register excerpt; signed UBO declaration in the bank’s prescribed form; notarised passports of all natural-person UBOs and signatories; corporate register extracts or certificates of incumbency from each offshore jurisdiction in the ownership chain; an ownership diagram evidencing direct percentages; audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements of the direct shareholders; and a legal opinion from a Swiss attorney-at-law confirming ultimate ownership and control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk or non-treaty jurisdiction tax residence of the parent shareholder, raising tax-transparency and source-of-wealth concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificates of tax residence (Form 85 equivalents) from each shareholder jurisdiction; double taxation treaty analysis prepared by a Swiss tax adviser; apostilled powers of attorney and board resolutions; source-of-funds declarations referencing disclosed bank accounts; parent company annual reports for the last three years; and confirmation that the capital injection consists of proven retained earnings or external financing from regulated financial institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IVD medical-device sector red flags arising from unregulated point-of-care products, unreviewed clinical claims, or missing Swissmedic notifications.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full business plan for the manufacture of microfluidic cartridges and immunoassay analyzers under ISIC 3250; ISO 13485 quality-management certificate or a documented certification roadmap; Swissmedic registration or import-licence confirmation for the IVD products; CE-IVD marking certificates and EU IVDR documentation; customs classification worksheets under HS 3822 and HS 9018; supplier and distributor agreements with named counterparties; and product liability and insurance certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow funding from a non-resident shareholder without a verifiable audit trail, triggering Article 7 GwG economic-background verification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank verification certificate of paid-in capital (Gründungsbestätigung / attestation de fonds) issued by a Swiss bank; capital contribution agreements (Übernahmeverträge) signed by each founder; shareholder loan agreements with repayment schedules; audited financial statements of the funding entity; a bank reference letter from the remitting institution; a formal source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declaration sworn before a notary; and third-party confirmation that no undisclosed lender or back-to-back financing is embedded in the capital structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons (PEPs) or sanctions-list matches on directors, shareholders, or downstream distributors in the IVD supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PEP self-declaration forms from all directors and UBOs; sanctions-list and negative-media screening reports from at least two independent commercial databases; narrative explanation of the source of wealth and business biography; independent legal opinion confirming no sanctioned involvement; evidence of termination or resignation of any problematic signatory; and a group-wide sanctions-compliance and AML policy adopted by the board of directors of the Swiss AG.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Share capital must be wired by SWIFT MT103 to the Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) held in the name of the Swiss AG at a FINMA-licensed bank, quoting the Swiss IBAN of the escrow account and the payment reference 'Einzahlung Aktienkapital / CO 634 / Sperrkonto' together with the date and number of the notarial deed of incorporation. The bank will verify the credit, match the total to the share-capital amount, and issue the non-transferable capital-verification certificate (Gründungsbestätigung) required for the Commercial Register. Additional paid-in capital (agio) must be referenced as 'Kapitalreserve / Agio / CO 634(3)' using SWIFT purpose category 'CAPT' (capital payment). There is no exchange-control permit; the only procedural burdens are the bank’s Article 7 AMLA verification of the source of funds, the SNB direct-reporting threshold (CHF 2 million external assets or CHF 1 million annual external flows), and standard sanctions/PEP screening before the funds are released from escrow.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements will be executed through (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier wire transfers in USD, EUR or CHF; (ii) irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600, with eUCP where electronic transport documents are used) for high-value imports of microfluidic components and export contracts to point-of-care distributors, with confirmation by a first-class correspondent bank where required; (iii) documentary collections (documents against payment or acceptance) for vetted recurring counterparties; (iv) the Swiss SIC and Instant Payment rails for CHF-denominated domestic payments and payroll; and (v) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant for EUR-denominated European trade flows. All payment instructions must reference the invoice, contract, and Incoterms 2020 rule; LC-drawn presentations must accompany commercial invoices, bills of lading, certificates of origin, Swissmedic/CE certificates, and evidence of conformity under the ISO 13485 quality system. Sanctions-list screening is executed on the beneficiary and its financial institution before each disbursement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC outright FX forward (FXA) in CHF/EUR and CHF/USD negotiated under an ISDA 1992 or 2002 Master Agreement with a Swiss commercial bank counterparty.
FX swap (FXS) for rolling management of short-term treasury liquidity across USD, EUR, and CHF positions.
Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) to hedge long-term balance-sheet exposure on trade receivables or import finance in EUR or USD.
Vanilla FX options (call or put) and zero-cost collars to protect forecast export receipts without speculative open positions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible only where a deliverable CHF/USD forward is impracticable; Swiss banks will quote them only with a documented hedging rationale and may refuse them for CHF as the fully convertible domestic currency, while SNB reporting obligations will apply to speculative NDF usage.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Federal, Cantonal and Municipal Corporate Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (competent for federal, cantonal and municipal corporate taxes in Switzerland)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, filing due no later than June 30 of the following year; cantonal extensions may apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest at 4.5% p.a.; late-filing fine up to CHF 5,000; penalties for tax evasion; compulsory tax assessment by the authority; enforcement proceedings including seizure of assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the VAT settlement period; for companies approved for annual settlement, file once per calendar year covering the prior year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 4.5% p.a.; late-filing fine up to CHF 5,000; administrative penalty up to CHF 20,000 for willful non-compliance; potential loss of flat-rate taxing status

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit mandatory if the AG exceeds any two of the following thresholds for two consecutive business years: total assets > CHF 20 million; annual turnover > CHF 40 million; 250 full-time employees on annual average. Ordinary audit also mandatory for listed companies, companies with public debt offerings, regulated financial entities, or upon demand by shareholders holding 10% of the share capital. If no ordinary audit is required, a limited audit (review engagement) is mandatory, unless the company has fewer than 10 full-time employees on annual average and all shareholders resolve to waive the audit entirely.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR Art. 958–959) requiring financial statements prepared under Swiss generally accepted accounting principles (Swiss GAAP), specifically Swiss GAAP FER; IFRS permitted for publicly listed or internationally oriented AGs; consolidated accounts for groups exceeding mandatory thresholds required under OR Art. 963.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Swiss AML Ordinance (GwG/AMLO), each non-listed AG must maintain an internal register of beneficial owners and must update it within 30 days of any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership. There is no annual UBO confirmation filing to the commercial register; however, the board of directors must verify the register's accuracy at least annually, and a written confirmation to shareholders is recommended as best corporate governance practice.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 12,000 depending on audit tier (limited review or ordinary statutory audit)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal corporate income tax (CIT) of 8.5% assessed on after-tax profit (equivalent to approximately 9.3% on pre-tax profit); plus cantonal and communal profit taxes, producing aggregate effective tax rates of approximately 11.9%-21.0% depending on the canton of residence (per Zug and Zurich benchmarks).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent box regime (qualified IP income may receive up to 90% reduction at cantonal level); R&D super deduction (up to 150% of qualifying R&D expenses in participating cantons); participation relief (95%-100% exemption on qualifying dividend and capital gain income from holdings of 10% or more); notional interest deduction (allowable on excess new equity in certain cantons); OECD Pillar Two Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax (QDMTT) applies from 2024 for groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cantonal combined corporate tax return (simultaneously serving federal and cantonal profit tax assessments), designated in German as 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen' or in French as 'Déclaration fiscale pour personnes morales'; filed electronically via the cantonal e-filing portal (e.g. eTax, SUPERPRO in Zug) or via approved Swiss DEC-certified third-party software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual tax return must be filed within six months after the end of the business year, extendable for up to twelve months upon written request to the competent cantonal tax administration. Federal and cantonal profit taxes are assessed in the same proceeding; quarterly prepayments of federal and cantonal corporate tax are due during the tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity identification: registered company name, legal form (Aktiengesellschaft), registered office (canton and municipality), Swiss UID number, and commercial register identification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should ensure the UID and seat are consistent with commercial register data; authorized representative in Switzerland for service of process must be identified where required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed schedule of shareholders, residence status, shareholdings in percentage, and amounts of paid-up share capital.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident shareholder, provide full name, country of residence, ownership percentage, and applicable double taxation agreement (DTA) entitlement basis to support dividend withholding tax (WHT) assessment and any treaty rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before taxes per the statutory financial statements prepared under Swiss Code of Obligations accounting requirements; must reconcile to the audited annual accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the Swiss AG is a branch or subsidiary of a foreign IVD group, reconcile Swiss statutory accounts with the group reporting package; no deduction of dividends or quasi-dividends is permitted in arriving at commercial profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses (e.g., excessive interest, undocumented intra-group charges, unjustified reserves) and deduction of tax-deductible items not reflected in commercial profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intra-group payments for IVD microfluidic components, immunoassay reagents, and royalty/licence fees must be supported by contemporaneous OECD-compliant transfer pricing documentation and an executed intercompany agreement with documented functional and risk profile.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the deduction for qualifying dividend income and capital gains derived from a participation of at least 10% of the share capital of a subsidiary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign dividend receipts must be supported by Form R-103 (Swiss tax authorities) and the applicable DTA certificate of residence of the distributing entity to verify the 10% participation threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income from qualifying patented IVD technologies and microfluidic innovations; regional R&D deduction determined under applicable cantonal law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain a Swiss patent register extract and detailed R&D project reports demonstrating substantial Swiss R&D activity for ISIC 3250 to substantiate the cantonal patent box claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of prior-year assessed losses within the statutory seven-year carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses must be separately tracked for federal and cantonal purposes; a change of ownership or business restructuring may impact usability; file carryforward schedules with the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax credits and withholding tax recovery
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recovery of Swiss anticipatory tax and foreign WHT credits on investment income and interest/dividend flows.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach proof of underlying Swiss 35% anticipatory tax (Form 118) and foreign DTA credit forms; non-resident lenders claiming treaty-reduced Swiss interest WHT must provide a certificate of residence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: procedural fines up to CHF 10,000 per canton, increasing to CHF 50,000 for repeat violations, plus default interest at 3.5%-4.5% per annum on unpaid assessed tax. Non-filing may lead to compulsory assessment, refusal of loss carryforwards, and initiation of collection proceedings (Betreibung). Wilful concealment triggers evasion fines up to three times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividend distributions by an Aktiengesellschaft, regardless of the residence of the shareholder; refundable to Swiss residents and subject to treaty reduction for non-residents at rates generally ranging from 0% to 15% depending on DTA and shareholding percentage.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must obtain an official Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the home jurisdiction and file a refund application with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) on Form 823 or the relevant DTA-specific form. Filing must occur within three years after the calendar year of the dividend distribution. For reduced treaty rates on future dividends, a separate authorization (Vorauszahlungsbewilligung) may be obtained whereby the paying company applies the reduced rate upon receipt of the TRC, subject to annual revalidation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: no Swiss withholding tax is levied on licence fees and royalties paid cross-border (0%). Interest: no WHT on ordinary intercompany loans or bank deposits; the Swiss 35% anticipatory tax applies only to interest on Swiss-issued bonds and money market instruments, reducible under DTA to rates generally of 0%-10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Swiss transfer pricing documentation (Local File) is required for taxpayers classified as 'large' for Swiss tax purposes (annual turnover exceeding CHF 50 million, balance sheet total exceeding CHF 20 million, or more than 200 full-time employees) or when annual cross-border intra-group goods/services transactions exceed CHF 10 million. A Master File is required for Swiss entities that are members of a multinational group with consolidated group turnover exceeding CHF 50 million, in line with OECD BEPS Action 13 standards.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply offshore-type Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); however, substantive economic substance is mandatory through the Swiss General Anti-Abuse Rule (Statutenwechsel doctrine), treaty abuse prohibitions under Art. 22 of the OECD Model, and the Steuerdomizilwechsel regime for migration to low-tax jurisdictions. A Swiss AG manufacturing IVD microfluidic cartridges and analyzers must demonstrate real entrepreneurial functions (production, warehousing, R&D, strategic management) and adequate substance in Switzerland to retain treaty benefits, patent box claims, and QDMTT compliance under Pillar Two from 2024.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful under-declaration of taxable profit, concealment of foreign IVD distributor sales, falsification of books or intercompany invoices, or omission of Swiss-source assets/income to materially reduce the taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 175 DBG, a fine of up to three times the amount of the evaded federal tax plus statutory interest; cantonal penalties of comparable magnitude; criminal prosecution for fraud in the event of forged documentation. Repeat or aggravated violations may result in publication of the final assessment and disqualification from reliefs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable as principals or accomplices; penalties include imprisonment for up to 36 months and fines. Where the board ordered, participated in, or negligently failed to prevent the false declaration, personal joint and several liability for the unpaid corporate tax and penalties may be asserted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to deduct, declare, or remit the Swiss 35% anticipatory tax on dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders or on Swiss bond interest; misuse of the DTA refund procedure through false certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment against the company of the uncollected 35% anticipatory tax plus default interest; administrative fines up to CHF 100,000; criminal prosecution under the Swiss Withholding Tax Act (VStG Art. 64); publication of the judgement in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members are personally liable for remittance of uncollected anticipatory tax; in serious criminal investigations, travel restrictions, provisional confiscation of passports, and asset freezes may be imposed; in egregious cases directors face imprisonment of up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating artificial losses or low margins through non-arm's-length pricing of microfluidic cartridges, immunoassay reagent purchases, or royalty payments to a related foreign entity located in a tax-favored jurisdiction; absence of contemporaneous documentation or intercompany agreements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of taxable profit on deemed arm's-length terms; recapture of group relief benefits; penalty up to three times the evaded tax for wilful conduct; late payment interest at the official rate; possible denial of loss carryforwards and order for amended filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing documentation or knowingly submit misleading Local File/Master File reports face criminal sanctions for tax evasion; civil liability for restitution of the adjusted tax and penalties; imprisonment up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal Swiss AG with no genuine business substance (no employees, no Swiss management, no real production of IVD devices) solely to claim Swiss DTA benefits, EU-Swiss dividend reductions, or the patent box incentive while the real activities are carried out abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and reclassification of the company as a conduit; retroactive obligation to withhold 35% Swiss anticipatory tax on dividends; application of the Steuerdomizilwechsel special tax on hidden reserves upon migration; penalties of up to 150% of added tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be ordered to cooperate in the tax reinstatement; personal civil liability under Art. 754 CO for issuing profit distributions without substance; repeated abuse may trigger travel restrictions and criminal sanctions for aiding tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Financial Crimes (Money Laundering / Mis-invoicing)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of the Swiss IVD manufacturing entity to route illicit proceeds through suspicious third-country invoices, mis-invoicing microfluidic exports to conceal proceeds of crime, cash payments above regulatory thresholds, or failure of a medium-risk IVD business to conduct appropriate customer due diligence on high-risk foreign distributors or payment via Swift LC/TT wires from opaque jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Swiss Criminal Code (Art. 71 StGB), confiscation of the proceeds of crime; penalty for legal entities of up to CHF 5 million; mandatory filing of a suspicious activity report with the Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland (MROS); potential administrative withdrawal of licences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face imprisonment of up to 3 years, personal restitution of laundered amounts, travel bans and passport seizure during proceedings, provisional freezing of personal assets, and disqualification from serving as directors of Swiss companies.
